recall.minute: Deep networks are trained by iterative optimisation. Mini-batch gradient descent updates θ ← θ − ηg with batches of 32–256; on the elongated bowl w₁² + 4w₂² a single η moves w₂ too aggressively and w₁ too slowly. Momentum accumulates a velocity v ← βv + g (β = 0.9) to accelerate consistent directions and damp oscillation, but needs a smaller η; Nesterov evaluates the gradient after a look-ahead. AdaGrad divides by the root of accumulated squared gradients and eventually stalls; RMSprop uses a moving average (γ = 0.9). Adam combines both moments with bias correction (β₁ = 0.9, β₂ = 0.999, η = 0.001) and moves roughly η per step; AdamW decouples weight decay. Learning-rate schedules (step, exponential, cosine) plus warmup, gradient clipping by norm (τ 1–5), the linear scaling rule for batch size, debugging from loss curves and early stopping complete the toolkit. Tune η first, then batch size, then the schedule.
